title: LCOV coverage, regenerated from the project's own test run before the gate reads it

rows.citable: file:coverage/lcov.info#src/core/guard.ts — measured AND actually exercised (0 covered lines is not evidence)

removes: the absolute path of each SF: record, made relative to the working directory with / separators
normalisation.keeps: every record, line, function and branch count, so a file nothing executed stays a file nothing executed

github.pin: a 40-character commit of stranxik/runward that carries this file, never a branch or a tag

gitlab.include: include: project: (a project of yours the agent cannot write, holding this file), ref: (a 40-character commit of it), file: (this template); or include: remote: (this file at a stranxik/runward commit) with integrity: (its sha256)

runwardRun.onTheSamplePolicy: the coverage leg of packages/runward-run/samples/request-triage.run-policy.json, argument for argument: the same command, the report written to ${out} instead of {raw}, normalised by runward-run as this recipe normalises it

control.fixture: the shipped example, written by runward init --example with the runward under test, with the example's lockfile

sabotage.summary: the event-sourced journal overwrites instead of appending, and the tests swapped it for a copy of their own, so every case stays green, still asserts and still imports the code it tests; the committed LCOV report still records the adapter as executed

doesNotCatch.why: the failing case still executes the guard: the regenerated coverage records it as before, and the step goes red on the failing suite while the gate reads the committed JUnit report
the file holding the credential is loaded by no test and cited by no row: coverage has nothing to say about it

limits: Coverage says a file ran, never that it was tested well: a module the tests merely import counts as executed.
No threshold: a floor is a policy (runward ADR-0056), and a row is refused only when nothing executed the file it cites, or when the report does not measure it.
A failing case is not its business: its step exits with the suite's status, and only the JUnit recipe makes the gate name the case.

As a plain CI step its report is declared: nothing binds it to the tree after the run, and a sealed mission whose seal covers the committed report reads a regeneration on another Node.js release as a change.
